newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends higher aided by corn/soy spillover.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends higher aided by corn/soy spillover.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed higher, supported by mill buying and spillover strength from CBOT corn and soybeans.
Dealers noted stronger demand from mills at the moment for higher protein wheats such as spring and HRW and less interest in lower protein soft red winter wheat.

"At the moment high protein is in demand and as long as that is, they (MGE spring wheat futures) are going to continue to gain and we (KCBT HRW wheat futures) are going to gain on Chicago (CBOT SRW wheat futures)," one dealer said.
September closed up 5-1/4 cents at $3.72-1/2 a bushel.
Other months ended four to 2-3/4 cents higher.
Iraq's purchase of 80,000 to 85,000 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter wheat for October shipment was also supportive. Iraq also bought an unspecified amount of Australian wheat.
Floor sources said Cargill Investor Services and FIMAT each bought around 1.0 million bushels of December. Benson Quinn sold 1.0 million bushels.
They noted that Monday's CFTC Commitments of Traders report was seen as slightly bearish as it showed that small speculators were the main long position holders in the market.
